metadata.description: Small organizational knowledge base for comparing retrieval strategies. Entities hold attributes only; all connections live in `relationships`. Documents carry free text and reference the same entities, so a text/vector pipeline and a graph pipeline draw on identical facts.

documents.title: Atlas Design Doc
documents.text: Atlas replaces the legacy keyword-only product search with a retrieval stack that understands intent. Product records are stored in PostgreSQL and embedded nightly by a PyTorch embedding service owned by Lena Okafor; the vectors are stored in Weaviate (see ADR-007). Ranking will incorporate click signals from the clickstream, which Atlas consumes from the Beacon Kafka topics, so Atlas cannot ship ranking v1 until Beacon is in production. Arjun Patel owns the search API, Tomás Rivera owns the React search UI, and Owen Gallagher is running UX research on query autocomplete. Sam Whitfield is the product owner. The embedding service is designed to be reusable by other internal consumers.

documents.title: Beacon Migration Runbook
documents.text: This runbook covers cutover of clickstream and order events from RabbitMQ to Kafka. Producers dual-write for two weeks before RabbitMQ consumers are drained. Airflow orchestrates backfills, and as of February 2026 all transformations are dbt models instead of the old hand-written SQL scripts. Primary contact is Hana Kobayashi. For consumer lag or partition rebalancing issues, page Hana first and Arjun Patel second; both have run the Kafka consumer groups in staging. Daniel Brooks owns the EKS deployment of the Kafka Connect workers. Airflow connection credentials are read from Vault.

documents.title: ADR-007: Vector Store Selection
documents.text: Context: Atlas needs approximate nearest-neighbor search over roughly 40 million product and content vectors. Options considered were pgvector on our existing PostgreSQL cluster, Pinecone, and self-hosted Weaviate. pgvector was rejected because load tests at 40 million vectors showed p95 latency above 300 ms, far over our 80 ms budget. Pinecone was rejected because contractual data-residency commitments to enterprise customers require that customer data stay inside our own VPC. Decision: adopt self-hosted Weaviate on EKS. Proposed by Lena Okafor, approved by Maya Chen. Consequence: the Data & ML team takes on operational ownership of Weaviate.

documents.title: Security Policy: Secrets Management
documents.text: Effective immediately, no new service may store credentials in environment files or CI variables. All production services must read secrets from HashiCorp Vault by June 30, 2026. Short-lived dynamic credentials are preferred for databases. Exceptions require written approval from the Security Engineer. Policy author: Fatima Al-Sayed. Approved by Maya Chen. The rollout program is tracked as Project Citadel. Teams currently in flight, including Beacon, must migrate their Airflow and Kafka credentials as part of the rollout.

documents.title: Q2 2026 Platform Planning Notes
documents.text: Attendees: Maya Chen, Daniel Brooks, Fatima Al-Sayed, Arjun Patel. Citadel is behind schedule with 23 services still to migrate. Platform has one SRE, so we cannot run Citadel and Drift in parallel. Decision: Drift is paused effective today, and Daniel moves to Citadel full-time. Grafana dashboards stay as they are until Drift resumes. Revisit Drift at Q3 planning.

documents.title: Echo Product Requirements
documents.text: Echo is an internal assistant that answers employee questions using design docs, ADRs, runbooks, and meeting notes. It reuses the Atlas embedding service and stores its index in Weaviate; ingestion jobs run on Airflow. Echo's model API keys are issued through Vault under the Citadel standard. Out of scope: HR, compensation, and performance documents are excluded from the index (decision of May 12, 2026, made by Priya Nair after consulting Fatima Al-Sayed on privacy risk). Questions about benefits or leave policy should be redirected to the HR portal. Lead: Priya Nair. Contributors: Lena Okafor (retrieval quality and LLM evaluation), Hana Kobayashi (ingestion), Fatima Al-Sayed (access controls). Beta target: September 30, 2026.

documents.title: Weekly Product & Platform Sync — 2026-05-18
documents.text: Attendees: Sam Whitfield, Hana Kobayashi, Lena Okafor, Arjun Patel, Maya Chen. Hana reported that Beacon cutover is slipping from April 30 to July 15. Root cause: the schema registry rejected several Avro schemas as backward-incompatible, and order events need to be re-versioned. Lena noted Atlas ranking v1 depends on Beacon click events and cannot launch in June without them. Sam proposed moving the Atlas launch to mid-August to leave four weeks of ranking tuning after Beacon goes live. Action: Sam to confirm the new date by Wednesday.

documents.title: Citadel Retrospective
documents.text: Citadel completed on June 30, 2026. In total 142 secrets across 23 services were migrated into Vault, and database credentials for 9 services now use dynamic leases. What went wrong: on May 6, 2026, a rotation of the Airflow metadata credentials broke Beacon's Airflow connections for about three hours because the old secret was revoked before workers picked up the new one. Lesson: rotations now happen in two stages with an overlap window. Daniel Brooks ran the migration tooling through GitHub Actions and EKS; Fatima Al-Sayed owned policy and reviews.

documents.title: Platform Team Onboarding Guide
documents.text: Welcome to Platform. Services run on AWS EKS and infrastructure is managed with Terraform. CI/CD runs on GitHub Actions. Dashboards and alerts live in Grafana; Daniel Brooks owns the on-call rotation. Request Vault access from Fatima Al-Sayed during your first week. Platform reports to Maya Chen. Designers share specs in Figma; Owen Gallagher and Tomás Rivera keep the shared component library in sync.

documents.title: Atlas Search Relevance Experiment Report
documents.text: We compared three retrieval strategies on 2,400 labeled queries. BM25 alone scored nDCG@10 of 0.54, vector search alone scored 0.61, and a hybrid of BM25 plus vectors merged with reciprocal rank fusion scored 0.68. Vector-only search failed badly on exact-match queries such as SKU numbers and part codes, which BM25 handled well. Recommendation: ship hybrid search. Authors: Arjun Patel and Lena Okafor. Adopted on April 8, 2026.

documents.title: Q3 2026 Platform Planning Notes
documents.text: Attendees: Maya Chen, Daniel Brooks, Fatima Al-Sayed. Citadel is on track to finish by June 30. Decision: Drift resumes in Q4 2026, starting October 5, with Daniel Brooks as lead. This replaces the March decision to pause Drift. First milestone is distributed tracing for the Atlas search API and Beacon consumers.
